claims.text: A conformal nanoscale ALD Ni or Cu–Ni coating on tungsten before copper infiltration will suppress void formation.
The ALD coating will suppress phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
The intervention will produce more uniformly bonded W–Cu interfaces than vapor-coated powder sintering.
The ALD-treated composite will have improved thermal transport relative to vapor-coated powder sintering.
The ALD-treated composite will preserve mechanical durability relative to vapor-coated powder sintering.
The ALD layer acts as an interfacial binder between tungsten and copper.
The ALD layer enhances wetting between tungsten and copper.
Enhanced wetting reduces interfacial microvoids and discontinuities.
The ALD coating promotes a graded interfacial bond between tungsten and copper.
Improved wettability and graded bonding facilitate complete copper infiltration and a stronger W–Cu diffusion bond.
Reducing voids and phase separation preserves continuous thermal-conduction paths in the composite.
The ALD-treated composite will show a statistically significant reduction in interfacial void fraction relative to the baseline.
The ALD-treated composite will show improved and more spatially uniform thermal conductivity relative to the baseline.
The ALD-treated composite will retain mechanical durability during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Vapor-coated tungsten powder sintering produces near-perfect contact between constituents.
Vapor-coated and sintered W–Cu composites still develop some voids under service conditions.
The intervention is expected to remain effective at service temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C under irradiation.
The intervention's benefits may diminish outside the stated processing or service-temperature limits.
